Sounds like what you are looking for is a way to inject some honesty into the conversation, yet without revealing your true beliefs.

One way to do that, which might work well for you, is what I call "asymmetrical absurdity" or for a less gay phrase, "shitposting your way into the leftard's heart".

It mostly just requires a lot of distasteful homework, which hopefully you can laugh your way through. Your homework is to know enough leftist "logic and theory" plus news soundbites, to be able to verbally run circles around your yuppy customers. You have to be able to one-up them. So when they tell you about "drag queen story hour" you can make an impassioned declaration that it's still not enough to combat heteronormativity. And should the need or opportunity arise, you have talking points locked and loaded, so you can rattle them off at a moment's notice with conviction.

And that conviction dovetails into the asymmetry part which is where the actual skill and hence satisfaction of this technique starts to enter in to the picture. Like men sometimes get into pissing contests about who is better or worse at what, leftists get into virtue signalling contests where their moral reputation is on the line. But unlike the men who are hopefully aware how fucking retarded they are acting, leftists make it symbolically a matter of life or death: social inclusion. What the asymmetry refers to is that they are actually going to be putting their reputation on the line, but you aren't. But you have to convincingly act as though you are. And that is where the first real element of skill comes in.

It's a matter of emotional intelligence. Sometimes you need to show how angry you are about "all the injustice". Sometimes you'll want to show how sad or guilty you feel about some recent incident and your own failings and complicit position in the interlocked systems of oppression. Sometimes you need to be elated over some recent petty/fake victory. But the common thread is that what you are really doing when you make any of these expressions of emotion, is issuing a challenge to your yuppy customer---"Do you care as much as I do?" Of course you can't be seen as actually issuing a challenge. Just like leftists don't conceive of themselves as competing for status when they virtue signal, you have to do the same. I find the key is to keep your focus on delivering your challenge within a frame of "We're part of the same tribe. Aren't we? This is who we are. Isn't it?" Imagine that instead of challenging them, you're giving them an opportunity--an opportunity to demonstrate their loyalty to the perverse tribe of leftism.

This brings us to the absurdity part. If you've done your homework, you can push them just that one degree further than they had been prepared to go. "Drag queen story hour" would be much more effective if they brought some girls' clothes for the boys to wear and vice versa, right? And when your customer eagerly agrees with you, immediately rattle off some theory, which if it's obtuse enough doesn't even have to be related, to justify your position. If your customer hasn't heard this bit of theory before, you've gained the upper hand because they have to tacitly admit that you're winning the pissing contest, and thus defer to your superiority within the tribe.

And that will be your cue to unleash the move that takes real artistry: saying something so unbelievably stupid, yet so full of reputation-staked pathos, that your customer is faced with the choice of A) agreeing and looking like a total idiot, or B) rejecting you and having to defend their own leftist cred.

If the latter happens you can, at your discretion, be conciliatory ("at least we're on the same side") or go on the attack ("how can you not agree with me?"), depending on what you think will be better for business I suppose. The thing to watch out for is a real hardcore leftist who is hiding their own power level, and starts lecturing you with theory points of zir own. In this case the accepted leftist thing to do is express gratitude for correcting your flawed viewpoint.

If the former happens you can at the minimum, enjoy the laughter of your internal audience at this buffoon's mindless idiocy. But the higher art is to have them walking away needing to deeply question their own worldview.
